11. How can the nth Fibonacci term be found?
Only the required term needs to be calculated. The intermediate terms are generated internally but are not printed.
12. What is the difference between finding the nth Fibonacci term and printing n Fibonacci terms?

When printing n terms, all terms from the first through the nth term are displayed:

13. Demonstrate a complete, object-oriented approach to computing the Fibonacci series, highlighting the class definition and entry-point (main) method.
This program demonstrates both operations: finding a specific Fibonacci term and printing the first n Fibonacci terms.
14. What happens when Fibonacci values exceed the range of the int data type?
Fibonacci values increase rapidly. When a value exceeds the range supported by int, integer overflow can occur, producing incorrect or negative values.
For larger Fibonacci values, long can be used instead of int.
15. What are the five basic rules of object orientation?
The entire world is a collection of objects.
Every object interacts with other objects.
Every object belongs to a category, type, or class.
Every object has properties and exhibits behaviors.
16. What basic concepts of classes and objects should be understood before learning encapsulation?
Creating an object with a reference.
Creating an object without a reference.
Understanding when an object can be created without a reference.
